chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is generous with you, then be generous, and when He withholds from you, then withhold, and do not try to out-generous Allah, for He is the Most Generous.

key_terms.تُجَاوِدُوا: You strive to be more generous than
key_terms.جَادَ: To be generous or liberal in giving

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'out-generous' Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a dynamic reciprocity between divine decree and human response, urging believers to mirror Allah’s generosity with their own giving and His restraint with their patience. It cautions against 'out-giving' the Creator, affirming that while humans are commanded to be generous, Allah remains the ultimate and supreme Giver (Al-Ajwad), ensuring that human acts of charity are reflections of His will rather than competition with it.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Rafa’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High is benevolent upon you, so you be benevolent, and when He<sup>azwj</sup> Withholds from you, so you withhold, and do not try to be more benevolent than Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for He<sup>azwj</sup> is the most Belevolent’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Marwak ibn ‘Ubayd from Rifa’ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, gives to you generously, be generous to yourselves; when He withholds, you should also do so, but do not try to surpass Him; He is more generous than you are.”
